_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for the Central African Republic covering Bantu and Sara peoples, Gbaya and Banda migrations, slave raiding zone, French Equatorial Africa (Ubangi-Shari), Bokassa's empire, coups and instability, Séléka/Anti-Balaka conflict, and Russian Wagner Group presence.

ethnic_groups.name: Gbaya
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; western CAR; led Kongo-Wara rebellion; slash-and-burn farmers

ethnic_groups.name: Banda
ethnic_groups.notes: Central and eastern CAR; diverse subgroups; severely impacted by slave raids

ethnic_groups.name: Sara
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern CAR; related to Sara of Chad; agriculturalists

ethnic_groups.name: Yakoma
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern CAR along Ubangi River; Kolingba's ethnic base

ethnic_groups.name: Zande/Nzakara
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern CAR; historically formed kingdoms; related to Zande in DRC and South Sudan

ethnic_groups.name: BaAka (Pygmy)
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous forest hunter-gatherers in southwestern rainforest; endangered culture

ethnic_groups.name: Fulani/Peul (Mbororo)
ethnic_groups.notes: Semi-nomadic cattle herders; caught in Séléka/Anti-Balaka conflict; Mbororo subgroup

ethnic_groups.name: Hausa/Arab traders
ethnic_groups.notes: Muslim trading communities in northern and eastern CAR

natural_resources.notes: Blood diamonds fund armed groups; uranium deposits (Bakouma, French interest); timber (tropical hardwoods, illegal logging); gold artisanal mining; 'paradox of plenty'—extraordinarily rich resources, poorest people; Bokassa's diamonds scandal with Giscard d'Estaing

military.notes: Army largely collapsed; MINUSCA (UN peacekeeping, ~14,000 troops) maintains fragile security; Russian Wagner Group/Africa Corps present (replaced French in influence); armed groups control ~80% of territory; Presidential Guard only reliable force

debt_aid.notes: Among world's most aid-dependent; UN humanitarian appeals consistently; HIPC beneficiary; economy barely functions outside Bangui; barter economy in countryside

education.notes: Lowest education indicators globally; conflict shuttered most schools outside Bangui; 37% literacy (lowest in Africa); French-language instruction; armed groups recruit child soldiers

diaspora_migration.notes: Massive refugee production (745k external, 630k IDPs); Séléka/Anti-Balaka conflict 2013-present; Muslim minority fled to Chad/Cameroon; most displaced per capita in Africa

digital_economy.notes: Virtually no digital economy; among lowest internet penetration globally; Orange CAR primary telecom; Bitcoin legal tender (adopted 2022, largely symbolic, reversed); power outages constant; no tech ecosystem

current_leader.name: Faustin-Archange Touadéra
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Former PM; elected post-Séléka crisis; re-elected 2020; relies on Russian Wagner Group support

former_leaders.name: Barthélemy Boganda
former_leaders.notes: Founding father; died in plane crash before independence; 'father of the nation'

former_leaders.name: David Dacko
former_leaders.notes: First president; Boganda's nephew; restored after Bokassa but overthrown again

former_leaders.name: Jean-Bédel Bokassa
former_leaders.notes: Self-proclaimed emperor; coronation 1977; overthrown by French Operation Barracuda

former_leaders.name: André Kolingba
former_leaders.notes: Military ruler; Yakoma ethnic base; forced into multiparty elections

former_leaders.name: Ange-Félix Patassé
former_leaders.notes: Elected president; faced army mutinies; overthrown by Bozizé

former_leaders.name: François Bozizé
former_leaders.notes: Military coup leader; overthrown by Séléka coalition

former_leaders.name: Michel Djotodia
former_leaders.notes: Séléka leader; first Muslim head of state; forced to resign under international pressure

former_leaders.name: Catherine Samba-Panza
former_leaders.notes: Transitional president; first female head of state of CAR

910.name: Early Peoples and Megaliths of Central Africa
910.description: Hunter-gatherer Aka (BaAka) pygmy peoples inhabit the equatorial forests; early agricultural and iron-using communities emerge on the savanna.

sub_clusters.name: Aka Forest Peoples
sub_clusters.description: BaAka pygmy communities in the southwestern rainforest practise hunter-gathering; among the earliest inhabitants of the region.

sub_clusters.name: Bouar Megaliths (Tazunu)
sub_clusters.description: Megalithic stone monuments near Bouar; evidence of organised communities and ritual culture in western CAR.

920.name: Bantu, Sara, and Banda Migrations
920.description: Successive waves of Bantu-speaking, Ubangian (Gbaya, Banda), and Sara peoples settle the savannas and river valleys; decentralised chiefdoms predominate.

sub_clusters.name: Gbaya and Banda Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Ubangian-speaking Gbaya, Banda, and Ngbaka peoples migrate into the Ubangi-Shari region; slash-and-burn agriculture; small-scale iron smelting.

sub_clusters.name: Zande and Nzakara Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: Avongara-Zande expansion from the east creates hierarchical kingdoms in southeastern CAR; Nzakara sultanates develop court cultures.

930.name: Slave Raiding and External Predation
930.description: The Ubangi-Shari region becomes a major slave-raiding zone; Sudanese, Wadai, and later Rabih az-Zubayr devastate the population.

sub_clusters.name: Sudanese and Darfur Slave Raids
sub_clusters.description: Slave caravans from Darfur and Wadai prey on the peoples of the Ubangi-Shari savanna; dramatic population decline.

sub_clusters.name: Rabih az-Zubayr's Raids
sub_clusters.description: Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr carves a slave-raiding empire across Ubangi-Shari and the Lake Chad region before French defeat.

940.name: French Ubangi-Shari (1889–1960)
940.description: France establishes Ubangi-Shari as part of French Equatorial Africa; concessionary companies, forced labour, and the Kongo-Wara rebellion.

sub_clusters.name: French Conquest and Concessionary Companies
sub_clusters.description: French outposts along the Ubangi River; vast concessions granted to private companies; rubber extraction through brutal forced labour.

sub_clusters.name: Kongo-Wara Rebellion (War of the Hoe Handle)
sub_clusters.description: Gbaya prophet Karnu leads a widespread anti-colonial uprising against forced labour and head tax; brutally suppressed by French forces.

sub_clusters.name: AEF Administration and World War II
sub_clusters.description: Ubangi-Shari within Afrique Équatoriale Française; Félix Éboué (first Black colonial governor) rallies AEF to Free France 1940; post-war reforms.

950.name: Independence and David Dacko
950.description: Barthélemy Boganda's death in 1959; David Dacko leads independence; one-party MESAN rule; economic difficulties lead to military takeover.

sub_clusters.name: Boganda, Independence, and Dacko
sub_clusters.description: Barthélemy Boganda champions independence but dies in 1959 plane crash; nephew David Dacko becomes president; single-party rule; France maintains military presence.

950.name: Bokassa Regime and Central African Empire
950.description: Jean-Bédel Bokassa seizes power; self-crowns emperor in lavish Napoleonic ceremony; brutal repression; French intervention ousts him.

sub_clusters.name: Bokassa's Military Coup and Rise
sub_clusters.description: Colonel Bokassa overthrows cousin Dacko on New Year's Eve 1965/66; escalating authoritarianism and personality cult.

sub_clusters.name: Central African Empire Coronation
sub_clusters.description: Bokassa declares himself Emperor 1976; lavish coronation December 1977 costs a third of national budget; massacre of schoolchildren 1979.

sub_clusters.name: Operation Barracuda (French Intervention)
sub_clusters.description: France deposes Bokassa in Operation Barracuda September 1979; Dacko restored; Bokassa later tried for murder and cannibalism.

950.name: Post-Bokassa Coups and Instability
950.description: Cycles of coups (Kolingba, Patassé) and mutinies; French military interventions; democratic experiments repeatedly fail.

sub_clusters.name: Kolingba and Patassé Eras
sub_clusters.description: Kolingba's military rule (1981–1993); Patassé elected but faces army mutinies and regional rebellion; Bozizé coup 2003.

960.name: Civil Wars and Séléka/Anti-Balaka Crisis
960.description: Bozizé's rule ends with Séléka takeover 2013; Anti-Balaka reprisals; sectarian violence; French and UN interventions; Russian Wagner Group presence.

sub_clusters.name: Bozizé Regime (2003–2013)
sub_clusters.description: General Bozizé seizes power from Patassé; peace agreements with northern rebels fail; Séléka coalition forms.

sub_clusters.name: Séléka Takeover and Anti-Balaka Reprisals
sub_clusters.description: Séléka (Muslim coalition) seizes Bangui March 2013; Djotodia briefly president; Anti-Balaka (Christian/animist) militias retaliate; ethnic cleansing of Muslims.

sub_clusters.name: MINUSCA and Touadéra Presidency
sub_clusters.description: UN peacekeeping mission MINUSCA deployed; Touadéra elected 2016; peace accord 2019 partially holds; continued armed group violence.

sub_clusters.name: Russian Wagner Group in CAR
sub_clusters.description: Russian military instructors (Wagner Group) deploy to support Touadéra; accusations of human rights abuses; growing Russian influence replaces French presence.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
